Chapter 9. The Ongoing Struggle for Recognition.
Have you ever felt that restlessness—the ache that comes from being overlooked, even when you’re giving your all? It’s that sense that, no matter how hard you work or how much you care, your efforts just slip by unnoticed. This ongoing struggle for recognition isn’t new. It’s been woven into the fabric of human experience for as long as we can remember, shaping the way we move through our lives.
Picture someone who pours their heart into everything they do—whether it’s their job, their family, or their community. Yet, somehow, they rarely hear a simple thank you. Over time, that silence can really wear a person down. And it’s not about wanting praise for the sake of ego or vanity. It’s about something much deeper: the basic human need to feel seen and valued.
Most of us don’t realize just how powerful a little recognition can be. Think about it—a quick word of appreciation, a nod of respect, or just a moment when someone really pays attention. Those tiny gestures can make all the difference. They lift people up, giving them the spark to keep going. But when that recognition is missing, it sends a different message—one that says some people matter more than others, and some contributions just don’t count.
For women, and for anyone who’s ever been pushed to the margins, this struggle is even tougher. They face stereotypes, assumptions, and a thousand little ways their work gets minimized. Their voices might get dismissed, their presence overlooked, and their achievements quietly swept aside. But you know what’s incredible? They don’t give up. Time after time, they find ways to support each other, to celebrate small victories, and to carve out space in a world that often seems determined to keep them quiet.
When you really think about it, recognition isn’t just about handing out praise or rewards. It’s about fairness—it’s about making sure everyone’s efforts are truly seen and valued. When people feel recognized, they’re more likely to take chances, speak up, and invest in the community around them.
